implementation_notes: Kotlin uses the same JPA mapping as Java - @Inheritance(strategy = InheritanceType.SINGLE_TABLE) with @DiscriminatorColumn/@DiscriminatorValue on a class hierarchy - but Kotlin classes and members are final by default, so entity classes must be opened with the kotlin-jpa (all-open) compiler plugin for Hibernate's proxies and inheritance machinery to work at all. Property-based access with mutable, defaulted properties is the practical style; there is no Kotlin-native STI ORM, so the manual alternative is a discriminated entity plus Exposed/JDBC SQL with a when-dispatch over the type code. A Kotlin sealed hierarchy cannot be the mapped hierarchy itself, because sealed subclasses are final - keep the sum type at the domain boundary and the entity classes separate.
pitfalls: Without the kotlin-jpa/all-open plugin, final classes break Hibernate: proxies cannot be subclassed and inheritance mapping fails at runtime with instantiation errors, not at compile time.

val properties, non-null types and data classes fight the ORM's requirements (no-arg construction, mutable state, nullable columns); data classes also generate equals/hashCode over all fields, which is wrong for entity identity.
Sealed classes cannot model a JPA hierarchy (their subclasses are final by definition), so do not try to unify the mapped entities and a sealed domain sum type in one type.
The generated DDL makes every subtype column nullable - exactly as in Java - so Kotlin nullability annotations on entity properties document intent that the database cannot enforce.
